title: Ingredients of the Success-Type Personality and How to Acquire Them
coreMove: Treat SUCCESS as a diagnostic checklist: strengthen the weak trait, feed the guidance system accurate data, take motion, and keep mistakes separate from identity.

exampleSpecs.audience: Paolo, a team lead redirecting a harsh label
exampleSpecs.stakes: A group is turning the framework into a ranking instead of a repair list.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the SUCCESS acronym as a diagnostic checklist rather than a moral rank.

exampleSpecs.audience: Bilal, a reader converting vague ambition into a target
exampleSpecs.stakes: Without a goal, effort keeps wobbling into self-criticism.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the bicycle analogy making direction practical.

exampleSpecs.audience: Brynn, an analyst separating facts from fear
exampleSpecs.stakes: A product decision will be distorted if the feedback signal is distorted.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use guidance-system communication to separate incoming data from emotional distortion.

exampleSpecs.domain: hotel bar before a pitch call
exampleSpecs.audience: Gerald, a presenter choosing internal courage
exampleSpecs.stakes: A nervous presenter may outsource courage instead of practicing action under risk.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show alcohol as borrowed courage and replace it with a concrete act.

exampleSpecs.audience: Pierre, a parent rebuilding confidence after a tense week
exampleSpecs.stakes: Only rehearsing errors is teaching the mechanism a false record.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use SUCCESS as a seven-trait checklist and rebuild confidence from remembered success.

exampleSpecs.audience: Everly, a writer separating an error from identity
exampleSpecs.stakes: A correctable behavior is about to harden into a self-image verdict.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use self-acceptance to separate behavior from identity while still correcting the behavior.
